questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an important function of the Supreme Court?

options.text: It acts to check on executive authorities and enforce the rule of law
It maintains of land records and revenue collection
It is the protector and guarantor of fundamental rights

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It maintains of land records and revenue collection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court** of India has several important functions, but **maintaining land records and revenue collection** is not one of them.
 
• The responsibility for maintaining land records and revenue collection typically falls under the purview of **state governments** and their respective **revenue departments**.
 
• The primary functions of the Supreme Court include:
 
 
• **Judicial Review**: It acts to check the powers of the executive and legislative branches and ensure laws are consistent with the Constitution.
 
• **Federal Equilibrium**: It ensures the balance of power between the central and state governments.
 
• **Protection of Fundamental Rights**: It acts as the guardian of the fundamental rights of citizens enshrined in the Constitution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **It acts to check on executive authorities and enforce the rule of law**__

 __
 
• The Supreme Court has the power of **Judicial Review**, allowing it to invalidate laws and executive actions that violate the Constitution.
 
• This function ensures the **enforcement of the rule of law** and prevents misuse of power by the executive.
 
 
 
• **It maintains federal equilibrium**__
 __
 
• The Supreme Court has the authority to resolve disputes between **states and the central government**.
 
• This function maintains **federal balance** and prevents conflicts of jurisdiction.
 
 
 
• **It is the protector and guarantor of fundamental rights**__
 
 
• The Supreme Court ensures that the **fundamental rights** of citizens are not violated by the state or any other authority.
 
• It has the power to issue **writs** for the enforcement of these rights.

questions.question: Which of the following is/are the highest judiciary in India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Supreme Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court** is the highest judicial authority in India and is also known as the **Apex Court**.
 
• It was established under **Article 124** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The Supreme Court serves as the final interpreter of the **Constitution**, ensuring the protection of fundamental rights of citizens.
 
• It has the power of **judicial review** to examine the constitutionality of laws and executive orders.
 
• The Supreme Court has original, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction as defined under the Constitution.
 
• The Chief Justice of India (CJI) is the head of the Supreme Court, and as of now, it comprises **34 judges, including the CJI**.
 
• Important cases such as disputes between states, or between states and the central government, are adjudicated by the Supreme Court.
 
• The Supreme Court is located in **New Delhi**, India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **District Courts**__

 __
 
• The **District Courts** are subordinate courts that operate at the district level in India.
 
• They primarily handle **civil and criminal cases** within their jurisdiction.
 
• They are supervised by the respective **High Court** of the state.
 
 
 
• **High Courts**__
 __
 
• The **High Courts** are the principal civil courts of original jurisdiction in each state and union territory.
 
• There are **25 High Courts** in India as of now.
 
• They oversee the administration of lower courts within the state or union territory.
 
• High Courts also have the power of **judicial review** and appellate jurisdiction.
 
 
 
• **Parliament**__
 
 
• The **Parliament of India** is the legislative body of the country, not part of the judiciary.
 
• It comprises the **Lok Sabha** (House of People) and the **Rajya Sabha** (Council of States).
 
• It enacts laws and amendments but does not have judicial functions.

questions.question: What is the upper age limit for appointment as a judge of High court as of October 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**62 years.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **upper age limit **for appointment as a **judge of High Court** as of **October 2022** is **62 years.**
 
• This limit was increased from **60 years to 62 years** in **2021** by the** Union Cabinet.**
 
• The **age limit **was increased to provide more opportunities for **experienced lawyers** to become judges.
 
• The retirement age for High Court judges is **62 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **57 years** is the **upper age limit** for appointment as a** judge** of the district court in India.
 
• **55 years **is the **upper age limit** for appointment as a** judge of the subordinate judiciary **in India.
 
• **60 years** was the **upper age limit** for appointment as a **judge of High Court** before it was increased to **62 years in 2021.**

questions.question: How many different levels of courts are there in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In order to maintain the supremacy of the Constitution, there has to be an independent and impartial authority that will decide disputes between the Centre and the States and interstate (among States).
 
• This function has been entrusted to the Supreme Court of India.
 
• The Constitution of India has provided a single integrated and unified judicial system for the whole country.
 
• It means that for the entire country, there is one unified judicial system.
 
• One hierarchy of courts with the Supreme Court as the highest or the Apex Court.
 
• It is also the highest and final interpreter of the Constitution and the general law of the land.
 
• It is the Last Appellate Court in India, whose top authority is the Chief Justice of India.
 
• High Courts, managed by Chief Justices of States, are the top judicial bodies in the states.
 
• District Courts are below High Courts (also known as Subordinate Courts), and are controlled and managed by District & Sessions Judges.
 
• They are further divided into Civil Court and Criminal Court.

questions.question: What is the retirement age of Judges serving at the Supreme Court of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**65 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The retirement age of Judges serving at the Supreme Court of India is **65 years**.
 
• This age limit is established to ensure a balance between experience and the need for fresh perspectives.
 
• Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed until they reach the age of 65, as per the Constitution of India.
 
• After retirement, former Supreme Court judges may be appointed to other judicial roles, such as in tribunals or commissions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**

 
 
• Article 124 of the Indian Constitution deals with the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court.
 
• Article 124(2) specifies that every Judge of the Supreme Court shall hold office until they attain the age of 65 years.
 
 
 
• **Appointment of Judges:**
 
 
• Supreme Court judges are appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Chief Justice of India is appointed based on seniority and consultation with other judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.
 
 
 
• **Post-Retirement Roles:**
 
 
• Retired judges may be appointed to various commissions, tribunals, or as heads of inquiry committees.
 
• They may also serve as arbitrators in legal disputes.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with High Court Judges:**
 
 
• High Court judges in India retire at the age of 62.
 
• This difference in retirement age helps to maintain a pool of experienced judges who may be elevated to the Supreme Court.

questions.question: Who does NOT fall under the executive of the Indian Union?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Justice of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chief Justice of India heads the judiciary and not the executive branch of the Indian Union.
 
• The executive branch of the Indian Union consists of the President, Vice President, Prime Minister, and Council of Ministers.
 
• Unlike the executive, the judiciary is responsible for interpreting and upholding the Constitution, laws, and delivering justice.
 
• The Chief Justice of India presides over the Supreme Court, the apex judicial body in India, and is pivotal in ensuring the independence of the judiciary.
 
• The separation of powers between the executive, judiciary, and legislature is a fundamental principle of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Executive Branch of India:**

 
 
• It is responsible for implementing laws and policies.
 
• Key members include the President, Prime Minister, and Council of Ministers.
 
• The President is the nominal executive head, while the Prime Minister is the real executive head.
 
 
 
• **Judiciary of India:**
 
 
• The judiciary interprets and applies the laws passed by the legislature.
 
• It consists of the Supreme Court, High Courts, and subordinate courts.
 
• The Chief Justice of India is the highest-ranking judicial officer in the country.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Powers:**
 
 
• A core principle in the Indian Constitution ensuring independence between the executive, legislature, and judiciary.
 
• Each branch has distinct roles and responsibilities to prevent abuse of power.
 
 
 
• **Roles of the President:**
 
 
• The President acts as the constitutional head of the executive branch.
 
• He/she exercises powers as per the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

questions.question: Which union territory has a high court of its own?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Delhi High Court was established on **31st October 1966.**
 
• The High Court of Delhi was established with **four judges, including the Chief Justice K.S.Hegde from Mysore High Court (now Karnataka High Court). ​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian judiciary is a hierarchy of courts with the **Supreme Court at the top, followed by High Courts for each state or group of states, and subordinate courts at the local level. **
 
• **Supreme Court:**
 
 
• **The Supreme Court of India **is the** highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.**
 
• It is composed of the **Chief Justice of India and a maximum of 33 other judges.**
 
• The Supreme Court has o**riginal, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction.**
 
 
 
• **High Courts:**
 
 
• Each state has a **High Court** which is the highest court within that state's jurisdiction. 
 
 
 
• **Subordinate Courts:**
 
 
• Below the** High Courts **are a hierarchy of subordinate courts including** District Courts, Family Courts, Labour Court, Industrial Tribunal, and others.**
 
• These courts deal with** civil and criminal matters of state and local levels.**
 
 
 
• **Tribunals:**
 
 
• Apart from the regular hierarchy of courts, there are several tribunals established in India for various** matters, including Income Tax, Customs, Excise, Armed Forces, Consumer Disputes, etc.**
 
• While these tribunals aren't part of the **traditional judicial structure, they play a key role in the Indian justice system.**

questions.question: The strength of Supreme Court has increased to how many judges as of 13 Feb 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**34**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The strength of the Supreme Court of India has been increased to **34 judges** as of 13 February 2023.
 
• This includes the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and 33 other judges.
 
• The increase in the number of judges aims to reduce the pendency of cases and expedite the delivery of justice.
 
• The last increase in the number of judges was approved by the President of India in August 2019, from 31 to 34.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Appointments**: Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President of India under Article 124(2) of the Constitution.
 
• **Collegium System**: The appointment of judges follows the collegium system, where the Chief Justice of India and a forum of four senior-most judges recommend the appointments.
 
• **Retirement Age**: The retirement age for Supreme Court judges in India is 65 years.
 
• **Jurisdiction**: The Supreme Court has original, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction, making it the highest judicial authority in India.
 
• **Pendency of Cases**: As of 2023, the Supreme Court faces a significant backlog of cases, making the increase in the number of judges crucial for faster resolution.
